title: Only 1,000 $50 World Cup Tickets for 8 Million New Yorkers—Here’s How to Get One!
summary: Imagine getting a World Cup ticket for the price of five fancy coffees! That’s exactly what New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is offering. On Thursday, he announced that 1,000 tickets will be sold for only $50 each. That’s a huge deal, because regular tickets can cost thousands of dollars. The catch? They’re only for New York City residents, and there are over 8 million people living there. The tickets are for seven of the eight games at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, which holds 82,000 fans. The one game not included is the final on July 19, where some seats are going for nearly $33,000! The cheap tickets also come with a free round-trip bus ride to the stadium. To get one, you must enter a lottery starting May 25. The mayor wants to make sure real fans—not ticket scalpers—get these seats. He said, “We are making sure that working people will not be priced out of the game that they helped to create.” During his campaign, Mamdani asked FIFA to set aside 15% of tickets at lower prices. FIFA had already offered some $60 tickets, but those went to national teams to give to loyal fans. The mayor’s plan is different—it’s just for New Yorkers. The World Cup kicks off on June 13, with group stage matches featuring teams like Brazil, France, and England. So if you live in NYC, cross your fingers and enter the lottery!
why_it_matters: This shows that sometimes local leaders try to make big events affordable for families, so your family might have a chance to see a World Cup match even when tickets are usually very expensive.

background_read: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico — it’s the biggest soccer tournament in the world.
Zohran Mamdani was elected mayor of New York City in 2025 and promised to make big events affordable for ordinary people.
MetLife Stadium in New Jersey is one of the stadiums where World Cup matches will be played; it can hold 82,000 fans.
Article_Structure: WHO: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the 8 million residents of New York City.
WHAT: A special offer of 1,000 tickets at $50 each, including a free round‑trip bus ride, available only through a lottery.
WHERE: MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, for seven of eight World Cup matches (not the final on July 19).
WHY: So that regular working fans are not priced out by scalpers or high ticket prices, and to make the event accessible.

perspectives.description: For people who love the sport, this is a dream come true — a cheap ticket to a World Cup game plus a free bus ride.
Some might worry that only 1,000 tickets among 82,000 seats per game is so tiny that almost no one will really benefit.
The lottery gives every resident an equal chance, so it’s random and not based on money, but it still means most people won’t win.
